units.summary: Test now builds a two-step breaker to match the new groupBreaker type. Constructor swap only; the test logic is unchanged.
units.headline: Reconcile-preserves-breaker test uses two-step breaker
units.reason: Test-only type swap to match the production breaker type; no assertions removed or changed.

units.summary: Test now builds the old breaker as a two-step breaker to match the new groupBreaker type. Assertions are unchanged.
units.headline: Changed-key reset test uses two-step breaker
units.reason: Test-only constructor swap to match production type; assertions unchanged.

units.summary: handlerEntry now holds a two-step breaker plus a per-handler watches context and cancel func. Reconcile uses these to end watches when a backend is replaced or removed.
units.headline: handlerEntry gains two-step breaker and per-handler watch context
units.reason: Struct fields added and breaker type changed, which alters lifecycle and concurrency behavior of served watches.
focus: every handlerEntry construction site sets watches/endWatches (tests build entries literally with nil watches)
endWatches is called exactly once per retired entry

units.summary: New constructor creates a cancelable watches context and a fresh breaker for each entry. Reconcile uses it for both new and changed groups.
units.headline: New constructor gives each handler its own cancelable watch context
units.reason: Creates a cancelable context per handler; a missed cancel leaks the context and leaves watches running.
focus: every entry created here is eventually passed to endWatches, including when reconcile returns early or errors

units.summary: The published snapshot entry now carries the breaker as the new two-step type and the handler's watches context, so serving code can tie a watch to its handler.
units.headline: Snapshot entries now carry the handler's watches context
units.reason: Struct fields changed on the entry that request serving reads; consumers must handle a nil watches context.
focus: nil watches context for entries built without newHandlerEntry

units.summary: The router now creates a router-wide cancelable watches context at construction, used to end all watches at shutdown.
units.headline: Router creates a router-wide cancelable watch context
units.reason: Introduces a cancelable context whose lifetime governs all watches; shutdown behavior depends on it.
focus: closeWatches is always called on every stop path

units.summary: Changed groups now get a new handlerEntry instead of being mutated in place, and replaced or removed entries have their watches ended after the new snapshot is published, so clients re-watch against the new backend.
units.headline: Reconcile replaces entries and ends watches of retired backends
units.reason: Changes replacement semantics and terminates in-flight watch streams when the backend key changes or a group is removed.
focus: endWatches runs after publish, so a re-watching client always lands on the new entry
anything holding the old *handlerEntry pointer across reconcile
breaker state for an unchanged key is still preserved

units.summary: The published servingEntry now copies the handler's watches context so request serving can bind watches to it.
units.headline: Publish copies the watches context into serving entries
units.reason: One extra field copied into the snapshot that the serving path uses to end watches; low risk but tied to watch lifecycle.
focus: entries built without watches (nil) are handled by serveWatch
